svg.aria-label: Three modes of transcription termination: why bacterial intrinsic termination needs both a hairpin and a U run, how Rho travels along the RNA to unwind the hybrid and how a ribosome blocks it as quality control, and the eukaryotic Pol II mode where poly-A signal recognition, cleavage and a degradation chase separate completion of the RNA from termination of transcription.
svg.text: A Bacterial intrinsic termination: BOTH parts are required
GC-rich hairpin
U U U U U U
Pol
1 the hairpin STOPS the polymerase 2 the weak A-U pairs destabilise the hybrid, so the RNA FALLS OFF
hairpin alone: stops but does not release · U run alone: does not stop
B Rho-dependent termination, and its quality control
Rho
ATP-driven travel along the RNA
catches the slowed polymerase and unwinds the RNA-DNA hybrid. No specific terminator sequence is needed.
Rho
Rho needs RNA not covered by ribosomes. Active translation blocks it,
so a transcript that is NOT being translated gets terminated and discarded.
Possible only in bacteria, where transcription and translation share one space.
C Eukaryotic Pol II
1 the polymerase passes AAUAAA
2 processing factors CUT the RNA
3 the upstream piece gets poly(A): mature mRNA
4 new RNA has an unprotected 5' end and is degraded;
when the degradation catches the polymerase, transcription ends
So the mRNA is finished BEFORE the polymerase stops: two separate events.
